weather_line: Fog at the hollow mouth · duck confirmed stationary · departure window narrowing

stories.headline: Departure Confirmed for First Light Saturday: Table Reaches Full Complement; Jeep Has Stopped Humming and Started Waiting
body: The kitchen table at the household nerve centre has reached what expedition planners are formally describing as 'terminal readiness.' As of Wednesday morning it holds the following, in order of acquisition: one ordnance chart (two circles, three margin notations), one trail guide with Steve's thumb crease at the creek-crossing page, one recovery rope, one set of annotated access-road notes with creek depth revised upward by Christine on Tuesday afternoon, and one hand-winch, which Steve has not explained further and does not intend to.

A departure window has been confirmed. Saturday. First light. Steve has written a time in the corner of the chart that he has since folded over, which the Prophet considers a navigational statement. Christine has already mapped the access road in two directions — inbound and, characteristically, out. The Jeep, sources note, has ceased its preparatory hum. It is now simply present in the drive in the manner of something that has decided.

stories.headline: The Duck Has Not Moved: Jellico Source's Token Remains on Mirror; Its Stillness Interpreted by Several Parties, Variously
body: The rubber duck left on the Jeep's driver-side mirror by the unnamed Jellico feed-supply counter source remains in position this morning, entering its second day of unbroken stillness. It is yellow. It is facing, according to the Prophet's best triangulation, north-northeast — which is to say, precisely toward Harlan's Hollow.

The Ministry of Magic has issued a supplementary note to its Tuesday bulletin, stating that the duck's continued presence constitutes 'an ongoing unregistered navigational advisory' and requesting that it be removed, logged, and submitted in triplicate. No one has done this. Steve has begun referring to it as 'the compass.' Christine has not corrected him, which in this household is a form of agreement.

stories.headline: Wednesday Handled Without Ceremony: Three Complicated Accounts Resolved; Griphook the Younger Accepts His Wednesday Briefing Under Visible Protest
body: Wednesday arrived at Gringotts in its usual fashion — without announcement, wearing the expression of something that expects to cause moderate inconvenience — and was handled by Christine before it had fully unpacked. Two outstanding interest disputes, one dormant vault reactivation, and a query from the Goblin Subcommittee on Seasonal Reconciliation were dispatched in sequence before the lobby fireplace had reached operating temperature.

Griphook the Younger, receiving his Wednesday briefing at nine-oh-four, reportedly accepted it 'under protest but without grounds,' which his senior colleagues have interpreted as progress. The Liaison Wing's running log now contains the word 'Saturday' in Christine's handwriting, underlined once, adjacent to no professional notation whatsoever.

stories.headline: Winch Investigation Conducted; Ellie Befriends It; Lucy Files No Report; Jersey Declines to Approach the Garage Entirely
body: The hand-winch retrieved by Steve from the garage on Tuesday evening and placed on the workbench has attracted the household's full familiar population, in three distinct and characteristic ways. Ellie approached it at approximately seven this morning, regarded it for some time, and has since positioned herself beside it with the air of someone who has made a new acquaintance and is not sure what they do for work but considers them friendly.

Lucy conducted a silent perimeter assessment at six fifty-eight, touched nothing, left no evidence of having been there, and is currently in the kitchen wearing the expression of someone who has already reached conclusions. Jersey considered the garage doorway from the hall, assessed the cold floor, the ambient chill, and the lack of any available lap, and withdrew. His position on the expedition itself has not been formally recorded.

familiars_corner: Lucy: Has reviewed the table's current inventory without touching any of it, noted three items whose placement she considers suboptimal, and said nothing. The winch is the only item she has inspected twice.
Ellie: Has decided the duck on the Jeep's mirror is a friend and visited it twice this morning. She has not determined whether it visits back, but remains optimistic on this point.

Jersey: Has located the warmest square foot of the household — a patch of Wednesday morning sun on the sitting-room rug — and intends to hold it through the weekend. He wishes the expedition well from this position.
founding_editor_note: That winch mount will need a reinforced bracket. I'd have used three-eighths plate, but I see you've made your choices. Safe trip. — D.

in_brief.sport: Household Strongwoman Division reports all gear staged, all weights metaphorical, and Saturday's load already calculated to the last ounce.
in_brief.forecast: Clear at altitude through Friday; fog returns to the hollow Saturday at dawn, as if it has been notified of the arrival and wishes to make an impression.

storyline_updates.title: The Second Circle
storyline_updates.summary: Day 4: The table has reached terminal readiness — chart, trail guide, recovery rope, annotated access-road notes, and hand-winch, all present. Departure is confirmed for Saturday at first light. Steve has folded over the corner of the chart containing the precise time. Christine has the road in both directions. The Jellico source's duck remains on the mirror, facing north-northeast; Steve calls it the compass. The Ministry has requested its removal in triplicate; no one has complied. Day 5 — the final day — is Friday, the eve of departure: the table should be photographed in the paper as a record, the Jeep given a final inspection, and the duck consulted one last time. Resolution should feel like the held breath before the wheels turn — everything ready, everyone knowing, first light almost here.
